sources.entry: wildduck - Scalable no-SPOF IMAP/POP3 mail server. (Source Code) EUPL-1.2 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: WildDuck is a scalable, no-single-point-of-failure IMAP/POP3 mail server that stores all data, including emails, in a sharded and replicated MongoDB backend.
summary.what_it_does: WildDuck is an IMAP and POP3 mail server built for horizontal scaling and no single point of failure. It uses a distributed database (sharded and replicated MongoDB) as the backend for all stored data, including messages. The README says the project aims to follow Gmail's product design, so when a design decision arises the default is to copy what Gmail does. The README links to a website, documentation, installation instructions, and API documentation, but the README itself gives no detailed feature list or setup steps. It is part of the Zone Mail Suite (ZMS), which the README describes as a set of programs and modules for an email server.
use_cases: self-hosted email server for a domain
scalable mail hosting on multiple servers
notable: Sharded and replicated MongoDB storage for all data, including emails
No single point of failure design
Product design follows Gmail as the reference
Part of the Zone Mail Suite (ZMS)
Offers an API with its own API documentation
caveats: Setup depends on running a sharded and replicated MongoDB cluster, which adds operational complexity
README gives no install commands; it points to external installation docs
License is EUPL-1.2, a copyleft license
